title: The Curriculum Dispute
location: Archbishop's Study — Cathedral of Saint Aldric

narrative.text: The Archbishop's study is exactly what you expected and nothing like it at the same time. Books line every wall — theological texts, histories, legal commentaries in three languages. The fire is lit despite the mild weather. Aldric Theron is seated in an armchair that is too small for him, leaning forward, his hands describing something in the air that his words are apparently not capturing. Archbishop Renek is behind his desk. He is listening. Or performing listening. The distinction is the whole reason you are here.
The curriculum as written presupposes certain conclusions about history.
The curriculum as written presupposes evidence-based reasoning. That's different.
Not a question. Renek's tone has not changed — it is still warm, still grandfatherly — but the temperature of the room has dropped slightly. Theron pauses. The pause is longer than it needs to be.

Renek notices you in the doorway before Theron does. His expression shifts — the argument is folded away, replaced by the practiced welcome of a man who has spent forty years receiving people in this room and knows exactly how long a silence should last before it becomes rude.
